lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.23 - A Listen and number

details: Listen and number checks understanding of key vocabulary by linking what students hear to the correct images. Numbering supports sound–image association and strengthens recognition of familiar activity words.
Look for careful listening, accurate numbering of each activity and consistent matching of spoken actions to the correct picture.
“We’re at camp today with some new friends! Can you listen carefully and say what each one has with them or what they want?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

details: Listen and choose develops listening comprehension skills by having students compare what they hear with visual options.
Look for careful listening, correct responses based on the audiotrack and good comprehension.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.77 - A Look and match

details: Look and match checks understanding of key vocabulary by linking each sentence to the correct picture. Matching reinforces meaning and supports early reading comprehension.
Look for correct matching of each sentence to the correct child, accurate recognition of target vocabulary, and students using picture clues to support understanding.
“It’s nearly lunch time and some our friends are hungry while others are finishing crafts. What are they thinking about eating and doing?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.24 - C. Listen and read

details: Listen and read develops key listening and reading comprehension by helping students follow the story while hearing the correct pronunciation. Reading allows students to practise their pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, eyes on the text and accurate tracking of the words.
“Now it is lunchtime! Who is eating what?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.24 - D. Choose the correct answers 10m]

details: Choose the correct answers helps students with reading comprehension, allowing them to show understanding of the text by choosing or writing the correct answer.
Look for correct choices or written answers, a good understanding of the text in C, and neat bookwork.
